# nForge

> nForge (Nano Forge, module `github.com/ams-soft/nforge`, by AMS Software e Consultoria LTDA, MIT) is a small, opinionated Go 1.27+ application runtime, built first for HTTP APIs: explicitly registered modules wired by typed capabilities and orchestrated by package `app` (HTTP is optional; worker-only and mixed applications share one lifecycle). One `config.yaml` drives layered configuration, `log/slog` logging (terminal and OpenTelemetry), OpenTelemetry tracing with `request_id == trace_id`, a JSON/CBOR/XML codec driven by one struct, an HTTP server on `github.com/ams-soft/go-ams-router` with a standard response envelope, typed routes validated before and after the handler, generated OpenAPI 3.1 docs and static files / single-page applications served from a directory or `embed.FS`, PostgreSQL (pgx + Squirrel) with multi-tenancy, JOSE/JWT bearer authentication, Redis or in-memory cache, RabbitMQ messaging with confirmed publishing and ingress consumers, and user-targeted Server-Sent Events (memory or RabbitMQ driver). Standalone packages add cryptographic primitives (`ncrypto`) a money helper (`safecalc`) and a QR Code helper (`qrcode`).

Important notes for code generation:

- Import the HTTP package as `nhttp "github.com/ams-soft/nforge/http"` and the crypto package as `ncrypto "github.com/ams-soft/nforge/crypto"`. Inside nForge, `net/http` is imported as `stdhttp`.
- Business code never imports `encoding/json`, `encoding/xml` or a CBOR library: it goes through the application's Registry (`codec.Capability`, or `nhttp.Send*`/`Parse*` in a request). The `jose` package is the only deliberate exception (protocol JSON).
- Build an application with `app.New(cfg, app.Modules(logs.Module(), codec.Module(), database.Module(), nhttp.Module(), myModule))` and `a.Run(ctx)`. Registration is explicit: a YAML section of an unregistered module is an error, and `enabled: false` only disables a registered one.
- Application code is a module: `module.New("api", module.Definition{Requires: []module.Handle{nhttp.Capability, database.Capability}, Init: ...})`; read declared capabilities with `module.Require`/`module.Lookup` (undeclared access panics). A disabled module publishes nothing: `Lookup` returns `ok == false`, `Requires` fails `app.New`.
- `Init` allocates and registers (routes, handlers) but never accepts work; `Start` returns once active. Stop hooks release only the module's own resources; HTTP and consumers are ingress modules: started last, drained first.
- Server-Sent Events are the explicit `sse.Module()` (memory or rabbitmq driver): `Manager.Handler()` behind `nhttp.Authenticate`, `PublishToUser`; best effort, no replay, user-targeted only. Long-lived responses call `nhttp.BeginStream`; `http.server.handler_timeout` is opt-in.
- `metrics.Module()` is an optional Prometheus-format registry; the HTTP server, SSE, Messaging, the database pool and the cache register instruments when it is present, `http.routes.metrics` serves it. `nhttp.RateLimit(limit, window)` and `http.server.max_inflight_requests` limit load.
- SSE keys are `sse.UserKey(principal)` (issuer, tenant, subject), not the bare subject; a stream ends at the token's expiry after an `event: reauth`.
- RabbitMQ uses `message.Module()` for the connection and `message.Consumers()` for ingress; delivery is at-least-once, queue type/arguments need manual migration, and unacknowledged counts require the Management API (not used by nForge).
- Register every route and middleware (`Server.Use`) in an Init, **before** the server serves its first request; go-ams-router panics afterwards.
- Programmer errors detected at startup or route registration panic; request-time errors are returned. Startup failures of enabled modules are returned by `Start`/`Run` after a full rollback; only `main` calls `os.Exit`.
- Serve a built frontend with `server.SPA("/", dir, nhttp.WithSPAReserved("/api"))` and public files with `server.Static("/assets", dir)` (or the `FS` variants for `embed.FS`) in an Init: they return errors, the root SPA is only the router's last resort (it never shadows a route) and answers just GET/HEAD navigations with `Accept: text/html`; reserve every API prefix.
- Prefer the generic route functions: `nhttp.Post(api, "/users", func(r *http.Request, u User) (User, error) {...})`, returning `nhttp.Error(404, "...")` for client errors. `TGet`/`TPost` remain for handlers that write the response themselves.
- Everything in the codebase (comments, logs, errors, API texts, tests) is English.
- Build with Go 1.27.2+ (the repository pins `toolchain go1.27.4`); lint with golangci-lint v2.15.0+ (older releases cannot read go1.27.2 export data) and the repo's `.golangci.yml`.

## Docs

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the single reference, read it before generating code. The authoritative reference for contributors and AI agents: architecture, runtime lifecycle, every package, full configuration schema, conventions and known gotchas. If this file and AGENTS.md disagree, AGENTS.md (and then the code) wins.
- [README.md](README.md): project overview, features, install, minimal config, development commands.
- [_examples/README.md](_examples/README.md): the runnable examples, the local Docker stack and how to test them.
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT, © 2026 AMS Software e Consultoria LTDA.

## Packages

- [version.go](version.go): package `nforge`; `Version` read from the embedded root `config.yaml` (framework metadata, not an app config).
- [app/](app): the orchestrator: `New`, `Modules`, `Start`, `Run` (signals), `Shutdown`, `Status`, `Reload`, `Value`, `WithProcessGlobals`.
- [module/](module): the capability/DI graph: `Descriptor`, `Definition`, typed `Capability`, `Build` (configure, resolve, check; no I/O), `Runtime` (Init/Start, readiness, shutdown), `Scope`, `View`.
- [config/](config): the loader: `Load`, `LoadFlags`, `Document` (raw sections; reserved `env`, `app`, `prd_exceptions`), `Binding`.
- [logs/](logs): `log/slog` setup (tint terminal + OTel), context handler injecting `request_id`, the logger module.
- [telemetry/](telemetry): OTel resource, TracerProvider, trace-ID generator for `request_id == trace_id`, the tracing module.
- [codec/](codec): JSON/CBOR/XML `Registry`, struct tags, strict mode, required fields, limits, typed errors, `ByteSize`, the codec module.
- [http/](http): package `nhttp`: the HTTP module and `Server`, response envelope, typed routes, query strings, OpenAPI docs, auth, tenancy, security headers, CORS, health/readiness, JWKS, static files and SPAs (`Static`, `SPA`, `StaticFS`, `SPAFS`).
- [database/](database): PostgreSQL `DB` (pgx pool + Squirrel), transactions, multi-tenancy (RLS or column), the database module.
- [jose/](jose): JWS/JWE/JWT `Service` with configured profiles, keys, JWKS, reload/rotation, the jose module.
- [cache/](cache): `*cache.Cache` on Redis or a bounded memory LRU, `GetOrLoad`, tenant namespaces, the cache module.
- [metrics/](metrics): the metrics registry (Prometheus text format) and the metrics module.
- [sse/](sse): Server-Sent Events: `Manager`, `Handler`, memory and RabbitMQ drivers, the sse module.
- [email/](email): email module: synchronous SMTP `Client.Send` (one recipient, text and/or HTML, STARTTLS or implicit TLS with verified certificates, no retry, no queue, accepted is not delivered) and the independent `RenderMJML` (pure-Go MJML 5, no variable substitution, no includes).
- [scheduler/](scheduler): Cron scheduler module: five-field expressions, IANA time zone, parallel runs with an optional per-job skip cap, local mode only (no queue, retry or exactly-once), ingress lifecycle with no HTTP needed.
- [message/](message): RabbitMQ queues, confirmed publishing, concurrent ACK/NACK consumers, DLQ/retry, reprocessing and lifecycle modules.
- [crypto/](crypto): package `ncrypto`: XChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-256-GCM, HMAC-SHA256, bcrypt/Argon2id, BLAKE3/SHA-256, secure random, ULID.
- [helper/safecalc/](helper/safecalc): money as integer cents with exact formatting.
- [helper/qrcode/](helper/qrcode): QR Code encoder and PNG/SVG/Base64/Data URI renderers with rounded styles and a safe logo.

## Examples

- [_examples/basic](_examples/basic): terminal logging, HTTP, and in-memory typed CRUD.
- [_examples/complete](_examples/complete): opt-in HTTPS + HTTP/3 + 308 redirect (`config.https-http3.yaml`, local-only certificate), plain and typed routes in three formats, typed query strings, docs, health/readiness, JWT login, memory cache, PostgreSQL notes, RabbitMQ, crypto and observability.
- [_examples/jose](_examples/jose): JWT login, bearer authentication, scopes, `Principal`, nested tokens, JWS/JWE, JWKS, key files (`cmd/keygen`).
- [_examples/cache](_examples/cache): the cache module on Redis or memory: objects, TTL, NX, counters, raw bytes, `GetOrLoad`, CBOR, outages.
- [_examples/database](_examples/database): Squirrel + pgx repositories, transactions, error mapping, tenancy in column or RLS mode.
- [_examples/sse](_examples/sse): cookie-authenticated `EventSource`, user-targeted events on memory or RabbitMQ, route timeout opt-in.
- [_examples/email](_examples/email): app without HTTP: renders an MJML welcome email and sends it once over SMTP.
- [_examples/scheduler](_examples/scheduler): scheduler-only app with PostgreSQL: a stock job at 07:00 America/Sao_Paulo.
- [_examples/message](_examples/message): worker-only RabbitMQ producer, consumers and DLQ reprocessing.
- [_examples/static](_examples/static): an API, a built SPA and public files on one server (`Server.Static`/`SPA`), from directories or `embed.FS`.
- [_examples/qrcode](_examples/qrcode): `helper/qrcode` gallery (PNG, SVG, Base64, Data URI, logo) and a QR Code printed in the terminal.
- Each example keeps its environment examples locally; examples with Docker dependencies have a per-folder `docker-compose.yml` (JOSE needs no services).

## Optional

- [_examples/observability](_examples/observability): Collector, Tempo, Loki and Grafana configuration (dashboard *nForge · Logs*).
- [http/internal/openapi/docs.html](http/internal/openapi/docs.html): the embedded Swagger UI page template.
